claims.text: The as-cast TaNbHfZrTi high-entropy superconductor has high chemical disorder.
Controlled annealing followed by rapid quenching reduces chemical disorder in TaNbHfZrTi.
Controlled annealing induces local short-range chemical ordering in TaNbHfZrTi.
Local short-range ordering optimizes electron–phonon coupling.
Optimized electron–phonon coupling enhances the superconducting transition temperature.
The annealing-induced ordering enhances critical current density.
The proposed intervention uses annealing at 800–1100 °C for varied durations under an inert atmosphere, followed by rapid quenching.
XRD, TEM, and PDF analysis can quantify the degree of local chemical disorder and short-range ordering in the HEA matrix.
Reduced chemical disorder and local ordering modify the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The ordering-induced modification of the electronic density of states enhances electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling promotes more efficient Cooper pairing.
Annealed samples with verified increases in short-range ordering will show a systematic increase in Tc relative to the as-cast sample.
Annealed samples with verified increases in short-range ordering will show higher critical current density than the as-cast sample.
Excessive grain growth or changes in residual stress could independently influence superconductivity and confound the proposed ordering effect.
Grain-size evolution and defect generation may occur alongside changes in chemical disorder during annealing.
Failure of verified ordering to correlate significantly with improvements in both Tc and critical current density would falsify the hypothesis.
